I'm 63 this year, been on this land since I was 18 — forty-five years. Never went to school, but the land taught me everything I need. It's just me and my old lady now, two mouths, two pairs of hands, on 34 and a half mu. The kids left for the city long ago.

I divide it like this: about 24 mu I do wheat then maize, back to back, tight as a drum. The other 10 and a half mu I grow cotton. Been doing it this way for 20 years. Cotton is my insurance — some years grain prices stink, cotton saves me. Other years cotton worms eat me alive, and the wheat-maize carries us. You don't put everything in one basket.

Right now it's early October, time to get the wheat in. Here's how I'm thinking:

**Winter wheat — 24 mu**

I plant around October 10, same as my father did, same as Old Wang down the road. I save my own seed — red wheat, local kind, grows fine here. Why pay the shop? I till the land after the maize came off, spread my fertilizer, and drill it in. For fertilizer, I put down half a bag of that compound stuff — the 50-jin bag from the co-op — per mu before planting. That's my base. Then come March, when the wheat starts jointing, I look at it. If it's yellow, I topdress with urea — one 50-jin bag of urea per 2 mu. Sometimes I give it a second lick if spring is dry and it looks hungry. I irrigate three times: once after planting if the soil's dusty, once at jointing, once at grain filling. Pumping water costs me — electricity isn't free — but three times is what works. Any less and the yield drops, any more and I'm throwing money away. I spray herbicide once in early spring, that's usually enough. For labor, me and the old lady do most of it, but come harvest in June I hire a combine and a couple of lads to help haul. I got 420 jin per mu last year, I'll aim for that again. Maybe 450 if the Lord smiles on us.

**Summer maize — 24 mu**

This is the rush job. Wheat comes off early June, maize goes in within a week, sometimes five days. I buy hybrid seed from the shop — yellow dent, the kind everyone plants, about 3 jin per mu. Costs me but you can't save hybrid seed, everyone knows that. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then urea at big flare stage — about the same as wheat, maybe a touch less total. I irrigate twice: once right after planting to get it up, once when it's tasseling in July. If it's a scorcher maybe a third time, but usually twice is enough. I hire the tractor for planting — I don't have a planter myself — and hire help for harvest in late September. Last year I got 500 jin per mu. Hope for 480 this year, maybe 500.

**Cotton — 10.5 mu**

I plant this in mid-to-late April, when the soil warms up. I use saved seed too — been keeping this cotton strain for years. It's less fertilizer than grain: one bag of compound per mu at planting, then a handful of urea when it flowers. Cotton needs more spraying though — bollworms are the devil. I spray insecticide three, four times. Irrigate twice, maybe three times if it's dry. The picking is the killer — me and the old lady can't pick 10 mu by ourselves anymore, our backs aren't what they were. I hire pickers, pay them by the jin. Costs a lot but what can you do? Last year I got 250 jin of lint per mu. I'll be happy with 230 this year.

Money? I'm tight, always tight. Total I'm spending on all inputs this season is about 26,000 yuan. I could push for more fertilizer, maybe squeeze another 50 jin per mu out, but what if prices crash? I'd rather have a few thousand yuan in my pocket for when the old lady needs medicine or the pump breaks. That's how I've survived 45 years — never bet the farm.
